certification.name: AWS Certified Generative AI Developer - Professional

domains.name: Foundation Model Integration, Data Management, and Compliance

tasks.name: Analyze requirements and design GenAI solutions.
Implement data validation and processing pipelines for FM consumption.
Design and implement vector store solutions.
Design retrieval mechanisms for FM augmentation.
Implement prompt engineering strategies and governance for FM interactions.

domains.name: Operational Efficiency and Optimization for Generative AI Applications

concepts.name: Translate business requirements into GenAI architecture
concepts.description: Choose a solution pattern by balancing quality, latency, cost, data sensitivity, integration needs, and operational constraints.

concepts.name: Prototype with Amazon Bedrock
concepts.description: Use a small proof of concept to validate model behavior, prompt design, retrieval needs, and feasibility before production hardening.

concepts.name: Apply Well-Architected guidance to GenAI
concepts.description: Use the Generative AI Lens and standard Well-Architected trade-offs to evaluate reliability, security, cost, performance, and responsible AI concerns.

concepts.name: Benchmark and select a foundation model
concepts.description: Compare candidate models by modality, context window, quality, latency, cost, regional availability, safety, and task fit.

concepts.name: Decouple applications from model choice
concepts.description: Use configuration and routing layers so a model can be changed without rewriting business logic.

concepts.name: Design resilient model invocation
concepts.description: Use fallback, circuit breaking, retries, graceful degradation, and cross-Region inference when availability or quotas matter.

concepts.name: Manage custom and fine-tuned model lifecycle
concepts.description: Use SageMaker AI lifecycle controls, registries, pipelines, versioning, rollback, and parameter-efficient adaptation when managed FMs are insufficient.

concepts.name: Validate data quality before GenAI use
concepts.description: Check schema, completeness, validity, anomalies, and quality before data enters retrieval, tuning, or evaluation workflows.

concepts.name: Process multimodal inputs
concepts.description: Use services and preprocessing appropriate for text, images, audio, documents, and tabular inputs.

concepts.name: Normalize data into model-ready formats
concepts.description: Transform application data into the JSON, message, endpoint, or conversational structures expected by the selected API.

concepts.name: Enrich and normalize source data
concepts.description: Extract entities, reformat content, normalize fields, and clean inputs when this improves retrieval or generation quality.

concepts.name: Choose a vector store and repository
concepts.description: Select storage based on scale, search behavior, latency, operational model, metadata filtering, and existing data platforms.

concepts.name: Design metadata for retrieval
concepts.description: Store filterable metadata such as tenant, document type, time, access scope, or product identifiers alongside vectors.

concepts.name: Partition and index vector data
concepts.description: Use sharding, multiple indexes, namespaces, or hierarchical organization when scale or isolation requires it.

concepts.name: Integrate repositories with applications
concepts.description: Connect ingestion, object repositories, metadata stores, and retrieval components using supported AWS integrations.

concepts.name: Keep indexes synchronized and fresh
concepts.description: Plan ingestion, incremental synchronization, updates, deletes, and freshness monitoring so retrieval reflects source truth.

concepts.name: Select a chunking strategy
concepts.description: Choose fixed-size, hierarchical, semantic, or no-chunking behavior based on document structure and retrieval needs.

concepts.name: Select embeddings for the retrieval task
concepts.description: Evaluate embedding model domain fit, dimensionality, language/modality support, quality, latency, and storage cost.

concepts.name: Implement vector retrieval
concepts.description: Use a supported vector store and knowledge-base retrieval path that meets latency, metadata, scaling, and operations requirements.

concepts.name: Choose semantic, hybrid, and reranked search
concepts.description: Combine semantic and lexical retrieval or reranking when exact terms and semantic meaning both matter.

concepts.name: Transform and decompose retrieval queries
concepts.description: Use query expansion, decomposition, rewriting, or transformation to improve retrieval for complex questions.

concepts.name: Ground models with tools and external data
concepts.description: Use function calling, MCP, APIs, or tools when the model needs fresh data or actions beyond static retrieval.

concepts.name: Manage reusable prompt templates
concepts.description: Use Prompt Management, variables, versions, Guardrails, and reusable templates to standardize prompt behavior.

concepts.name: Manage conversation context and history
concepts.description: Selectively preserve relevant state, messages, summaries, and context while controlling token growth.

concepts.name: Govern prompt changes
concepts.description: Use approvals, logging, versioning, traceability, and controlled promotion for prompts that affect production behavior.

concepts.name: Regression-test prompts
concepts.description: Evaluate prompt changes against representative datasets and expected behavior before deployment.

concepts.name: Use structured prompting patterns
concepts.description: Use structured inputs/outputs, constraints, examples, role/context instructions, and reasoning-oriented patterns when they improve reliability.

concepts.name: Build prompt flows
concepts.description: Use Bedrock Prompt Flows to chain prompts, models, conditions, and processing steps into reusable workflows.

questions.prompt: A support organization wants a GenAI assistant over private product manuals. Answers must cite internal evidence, the first release should minimize infrastructure, and only later may it take support actions. Choose the strongest decision at each stage.

steps.prompt: Which first-release architecture best fits the stated need?

choices.label: Use managed foundation-model inference with RAG over the private manuals
Fine-tune a model first so it memorizes the manuals
Start with an autonomous agent that can modify support systems
Train a new foundation model from scratch

steps.prompt: What is the most useful early proof of concept?

choices.label: Prototype the prompt + retrieval path with Amazon Bedrock and representative manuals/questions
Build full multi-Region production HA before testing answer quality
Launch a large fine-tuning job without a retrieval baseline
Grant production write tools so the prototype can demonstrate automation

steps.prompt: What evidence should gate production hardening?

choices.label: Representative retrieval/answer evaluation plus latency, cost, safety, and failure-mode tests
One successful executive demo
Only EC2 CPU metrics
Only average output token count

questions.explanation: RAG is the direct fit because the knowledge is private, changeable, and needs evidence grounding; fine-tuning is not the first choice for keeping a document corpus current. A small Bedrock proof of concept tests model behavior and retrieval with minimal infrastructure. Production readiness still requires representative quality, latency, cost, safety, resilience, and operational evaluation—one demo or one infrastructure metric cannot establish that.
hints: Separate the knowledge-grounding requirement from future tool-use requirements.

questions.prompt: Complete the model-selection table. Type the model capability, limit, parameter, or availability constraint that the requirement points to.

need.template: Requirement: accept both text and images in the same application flow. Which model capability must be verified first?
Requirement: process very long retrieved/context documents without truncation. Which model limit is central?
Requirement: make outputs less random for a tightly constrained extraction task. Which common inference parameter is usually reduced?
Requirement: deploy in a mandated AWS Region. What must be checked before selecting the FM?

questions.explanation: Model choice is driven by the workload: modality support controls which input types the model can consume; the context window limits how much prompt/retrieved content fits; temperature is a common randomness control; and regional/model availability constrains where the application can legally and technically invoke the model. These are different dimensions, so a strong benchmark evaluates them separately instead of picking a model by brand or maximum parameter count.
hints: Use the requirement wording to identify the decision dimension before naming the answer.

questions.prompt: Build a model-input pipeline for messy enterprise records. Assign the component that best fits each role; some components are distractors.

slots.label: Convert accepted records into a consistent model-ready structure
Add required metadata/context before model consumption
Create the request/message shape expected by the model API

questions.explanation: A reliable FM-consumption pipeline validates quality before bad data reaches the model, normalizes accepted records into a predictable structure, enriches them with the metadata/context the application needs, and only then serializes the model-specific request shape. CDN and DNS controls are real AWS services but do not perform these data-quality/model-readiness roles.
hints: Think in terms of data quality → consistent shape → useful context → API-ready representation.

questions.prompt: Assemble the core roles of a governed vector-retrieval design. Each role should be filled by the component that directly owns it.

slots.label: Convert source/query text into vector representations
Constrain retrieval by tenant, document type, date, or other attributes
Keep the searchable index aligned with source changes

questions.explanation: Embedding, indexing, metadata isolation/filtering, and source synchronization are distinct responsibilities. The embedding model creates vector representations; the vector store searches them; metadata controls which records are eligible for a query; and the ingestion/sync path determines freshness. Generation temperature affects model output, not vector-store partitioning or freshness.
hints: Ask what produces vectors, what searches them, what filters eligibility, and what keeps the index fresh.

steps.prompt: The relevant chunk exists but ranks below noisy matches for queries containing exact product codes. What change best matches the evidence?

choices.label: Evaluate hybrid lexical+semantic retrieval and/or reranking
Increase temperature to make retrieval more creative
Increase max output tokens
Rotate the KMS key

steps.prompt: How should the fix be verified?

choices.label: Run representative retrieval tests and confirm authoritative chunks appear/rank appropriately before re-evaluating generated answers
Run one successful query
Check only CPUUtilization
Check only daily spend

questions.explanation: Debug RAG from evidence upstream to downstream. First prove the changed source reached the index. If indexed content is missing from candidates, inspect query transformation, filters, chunking/embeddings, and search configuration. If the correct chunk is present but ranked poorly—especially with exact identifiers—hybrid retrieval or reranking is a targeted fix. A larger model, higher temperature, or more output tokens cannot repair missing retrieval evidence.
hints: Do not change the generator until you have inspected the retrieved candidates.

questions.prompt: Complete the prompt-engineering table. Type the pattern or governance mechanism that best fits each requirement.

need.template: Downstream automation needs machine-validated JSON with required fields.
The model needs concrete demonstrations of the desired classification/format behavior.
The prompt contains trusted instructions, retrieved context, and user input that should remain clearly separated.
A prompt change must be reviewed, compared, and rolled back if it regresses quality.

questions.explanation: Structured output is for predictable machine-consumable shape; few-shot examples demonstrate desired behavior; explicit sections/delimiters reduce ambiguity between instruction and context; and prompt versioning makes changes traceable and rollbackable. None of these removes the need for output validation, authorization, or regression evaluation—the prompt is only one layer of the application.
hints: Focus on the purpose of the pattern, not on which prompt would be longest.
